name: represents-actor-tier
body:
`represents` is mandatory: the actor-tier chain (spine-backfill) [with user]. Supersedes global.note.represents-unused, which recorded 0 `represents` edges and claimed the model did not use the kind — that state was wrong and is retired.

Decision [with user]: `represents` is NOT optional. Every requirements.user must be represented by a solution.person, and every solution.person must represent a requirements.user.

Schema determination [autonomous]: a direct `represents` from a User to a Person is refused. Exact refusal:
  apg: invalid `represents` edge `requirements.user.deck-author` -> `solution.person.deck-author` — allowed shapes: requirements.user -> domain.entity; domain.entity -> solution.person
`CALL show_connection('Represents')` confirms the only shapes are User->Entity and Entity->Person. The schema-legal form of the user<->person identity is therefore the two-hop chain requirements.user.* -> domain.entity.* -> solution.person.* — the model's previously-recorded option (b), not a workaround.

Resolution [with user/autonomous]: added the actor domain tier — domain.group.actors (attribute generic) containing domain.entity.deck-author, domain.entity.template-author and domain.entity.maintainer — plus requirements.user.maintainer (see requirements.note.maintainer-user) and six `represents` edges:
  requirements.user.deck-author -> domain.entity.deck-author -> solution.person.deck-author
  requirements.user.template-author -> domain.entity.template-author -> solution.person.template-author
  requirements.user.maintainer -> domain.entity.maintainer -> solution.person.maintainer

Result (queried on this branch): 3/3 Users have a represents chain to a Person and 3/3 Persons have one from a User — 0 gaps in both directions.

Anchoring rule (correction [with user]): actor entities are anchored to the solution tier by `represents` -> solution.person.*, NOT by `realised-by`. The realised-by invariant applies to requirement-driven domain nodes (those a Requirement `drives`); actor entities are identity anchors, not requirement-driven, and are exempt. An earlier version gave each actor entity a realised-by to the solution container through which the role acts (the two authors -> solution.container.cli-binary; the maintainer -> solution.container.release-pipeline) and the group -> solution.system.kalide — asserting that a person/role is realised by the CLI binary or the release pipeline, which is false; those four edges existed only to satisfy an 'every entity has a realised-by' count and have been removed. The identity linkage to the Person is carried by `represents` (the only legal Entity->Person edge), not by `realised-by`, which cannot target a Person. See domain.note.actor-entities and global.note.spine-widened-invariants-audit (represents pass).
